channel.title: Daily Recap — 🏰 Disney News
channel.description: What happened in 🏰 Disney News, recapped daily from subscribed feeds.

item.title: Disney World's worst crowds in six months have arrived
item.description:
The extended slow season at Walt Disney World is over. After months of unusually low crowds — June through September ran almost uniformly uncrowded, with only occasional spikes into moderate territory — the parks have hit their busiest stretch in roughly six months. This summer was slow enough that the long-running debate about whether an off-season still exists shifted to whether the whole summer had become the off-season.

That lull has now broken, likely driven by fall-break travel, Halloween events, and the start of the holiday build-up. The timing is worth noting for anyone planning a trip: the window of low crowds has closed, so expect heavier wait times and higher demand through the rest of the year.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Disney World’s Worst Crowds in 6 Months Have Hit

item.title: Disney Cruise Line drops Palo's prix fixe menu, tightens Platinum and Pearl perk
item.description:
Disney Cruise Line is changing things at Palo, the adults-only restaurant. The popular prix fixe dinner is being replaced with an à la carte menu, and Platinum and Pearl Castaway Club members with upcoming sailings are being emailed about the change.

Separately, Disney appears poised to enforce a long-standing rule more strictly: the complimentary dining perk for Platinum and Pearl members applies to dinner only, not brunch. Guests who had been using the perk for Palo brunch may now be told to pay full price. If you're sailing soon as a top-tier Castaway Club member, expect a pricier Palo and book dinner, not brunch, if you want the free meal.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Disney Dropping Palo’s Prix Fixe Menu & Enforcing Pearl & Platinum Perk for Dinner Only, No Brunch

item.title: Halloween season rolls on at Disney Springs and Disneyland
item.description:
Disney Parks Blog rounded up this season's Halloween happenings at Disney Springs — shopping, dining, and entertainment offerings across the district aimed at families spending the day soaking in the holiday atmosphere. It's the standard seasonal playbook: limited-time merchandise, themed food, and festive decorations through the holiday.

Over at Disneyland, the Pixar Place Hotel is offering new Monsters, Inc.-themed Halloween wallpapers for mobile devices, joining two months of seasonal coverage across Disney Parks worldwide. The Halloween season at Disneyland Resort runs August 21 through October 31, so these are the final weeks before the parks flip to the holidays.

Sources

  • Disney Parks Blog: What’s New and What to Explore at Disney Springs This Halloween Season
  • Disney Parks Blog: New Monsters, Inc. Halloween Wallpapers from Pixar Place Hotel at Disneyland

item.title: Banana Ball returns to Disney World in spring 2027 — plus a new tournament
item.description:
Banana Ball — the viral, dance-party take on baseball — is coming back to Walt Disney World in 2027. The dates and locations for next season were announced live on ESPN2 and the Banana Ball YouTube channel during the Banana Ball City Selection Show.

This time there's a twist: all of the league's teams will compete in the second Banana Ball Open for a chance to clinch an early playoff berth, making the Disney World stop a tournament event rather than just an exhibition. Details include how WDW fans can score tickets. For Disney, it's another sign the company is leaning into event-style entertainment that draws fans outside the traditional parks calendar.

Sources

  • Disney Parks Blog: Banana Ball Coming to Disney World in 2027: What to Know
  • Disney Tourist Blog: Banana Ball Open Baseball Tournament Coming to Disney World in Spring 2027

item.title: Southwest is effectively killing the Companion Pass
item.description:
Southwest Airlines continues its radical reinvention: starting in 2027, more changes to the Rapid Rewards loyalty program amount to a 'metaphorical death blow' to the Companion Pass for many travelers. After two years of throwing out its decades-old, family-friendly playbook — assigned seating, new fare structures — the airline is now reworking the loyalty program that made it a favorite for Disney families.

The Companion Pass has long been the holy grail for Orlando-bound families, effectively letting a second person fly free. Its dilution is one more reason Disney trip planning math keeps changing: the era of reliably cheap Southwest fares to Orlando is fading, and families should price-compare rather than assume Southwest loyalty still pays.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: RIP Southwest Airlines Companion Pass

item.title: 10% off Disney gift cards via Google Play Fest
item.description:
With Black Friday about a month away, an early discount has appeared: the inaugural Google Play Fest is offering 10% off Disney gift cards for a limited time. Disney gift cards can be used across the parks, resorts, dining, and shopDisney, so a 10% discount is effectively a 10% discount on nearly everything Disney sells.

Savvy planners stack these: buy discounted gift cards now, then use them for holiday-season trips, dining packages, or merchandise during the Black Friday sales themselves. Watch the fine print on purchase limits and which denominations qualify, but for anyone with a Disney trip or Disney-loving gift recipient in the cards, this is one of the best recurring deals in the Disney ecosystem.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Save 10% on Disney Gift Cards for a Limited Time!

item.title: Coronado Springs begins a year-plus construction project
item.description:
Walt Disney World has added another hotel refurbishment to its 2026–2027 construction calendar, this time at Coronado Springs Resort. The current phase is confined to the convention center and probably won't affect most guests — but the work is expected to continue beyond what's currently calendared, with room refreshes likely extending into 2028.

Coronado Springs is one of Disney World's most popular convention hotels, and a refreshed Gran Destino Tower-era property will matter for the meetings business. For leisure guests: construction is part of the background noise of visiting Disney World now, but if you're booking Coronado Springs for 2027–2028, it's worth checking which buildings are affected before choosing a room request.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Year-Plus Project at Disney’s Coronado Springs Resort

item.title: Disney Cruise Line reveals the 'Disney Imagination' — the first Disney ship to sail from Japan
item.description:
Disney Cruise Line and the Oriental Land Company have revealed the name of the first Disney cruise ship that will homeport in Japan: the Disney Imagination. The announcement covers the first ship built for the Japanese market under the partnership between DCL and OLC, the operator of Tokyo Disneyland and Tokyo DisneySea.

It matters because this is a major expansion of Disney cruising into Asia — a purpose-built ship for the Japanese market, not a redeployment of an existing one — and it signals real ambition for DCL's international growth. There's also a fun open question in the coverage: whether Figment, the EPCOT dragon with a cult following, finally gets his due on this ship. More details on itineraries, theming, and timing should follow; for now, the headline is the name and the commitment.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: DCL Reveals Disney Imagination Cruise Ship: Is Figment Finally Going Global?!

item.title: Rose & Crown at EPCOT closing for a lengthy refurbishment through 2027
item.description:
Walt Disney World has quietly added a closure warning for Rose & Crown, the popular table-service pub and restaurant in EPCOT's UK pavilion, signaling it will close for a lengthy refurbishment sometime in 2027. A construction permit points toward a summer reopening, suggesting the closure will span much of the year.

It matters because Rose & Crown is one of EPCOT's most beloved dining spots — a longtime favorite for its atmosphere, fish and chips, and Illuminations-adjacent fireworks viewing — and a months-long closure removes a big chunk of the UK pavilion's draw. If you're planning a 2027 trip with your heart set on dining there, watch the closure dates closely; Disney's notice appears to have gone up with little fanfare.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Rose & Crown Closing for Refurbishment Until Later in 2027, Permit Suggests Summer Reopening

item.title: Winnie the Pooh turns 100: new anniversary merch and Pooh celebrations across the parks
item.description:
October 2026 marks 100 years since A.A. Milne introduced Winnie-the-Pooh in October 1926, and Disney is celebrating with a wave of centennial merchandise plus Pooh-themed experiences across the parks. The new product line leans into the anniversary with collectible items for the silly old bear, while park coverage rounds up where to find Pooh — from attractions and character greetings to honey-flavored treats — in the parks.

It matters mostly as a shopping and trip-planning signal: anniversary merch lines tend to sell out, and the parks are leaning into the centennial as a reason to visit. If you're a Pooh fan (or buying for one), the merch drop is the news; the park roundup is a useful companion if a visit is already on the calendar.

Sources

  • Disney Parks Blog: Discover Something Sweet with New Winnie the Pooh 100th Anniversary Products
  • Disney Parks Blog: Find Winnie the Pooh Across Disney Parks and More

item.title: Fact check: is Tokyo Disneyland really cheaper than Walt Disney World?
item.description:
In the wake of Walt Disney World's 2027 price increases, fans have been claiming they could visit an international Disney park for the cost of a WDW trip. This analysis actually runs the numbers — airfare, hotels, park admission, food, and line-skipping — to test whether Tokyo Disneyland is really cheaper than Disney World.

The short answer: it can genuinely be true, at least in some scenarios. Tokyo Disney Resort's admission and food prices are dramatically lower than WDW's, and that gap is wide enough to offset a trans-Pacific flight for some travelers. It matters because the math has shifted the conversation from grumbling into a real planning question — and because it underscores how far WDW pricing has climbed when a trip to Japan is now a credible alternative on cost.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Is Tokyo Disneyland Cheaper Than Disney World?

item.title: Disney names first Japan-based cruise ship: Disney Imagination, sailing 2029
item.description:
Disney Cruise Line revealed the name of its first ship to sail from Japan: the Disney Imagination. The vessel will homeport in Tokyo beginning in spring 2029, inviting families aboard what Disney describes as a ship powered by creativity and optimism.

The announcement marks a major expansion of Disney's cruise footprint into Asia. A Japan-based ship has been in the works for some time, and the naming gives the project a concrete identity — and a countdown. Expect itinerary details, bookings, and pricing to follow well ahead of the 2029 maiden voyage, so there's nothing to act on yet; this is a flag-in-the-ground moment for anyone planning a Disney trip to Japan in the next few years.

Sources

  • Disney Parks Blog: Disney Imagination Named as First Disney Cruise Ship Sailing from Japan in 2029

item.title: Six Ravens by Gideon's Bakehouse sets grand opening at Disney World
item.description:
Two months after its soft opening, the new Six Ravens restaurant from the beloved Gideon's Bakehouse team is holding its grand opening this weekend at Walt Disney World. The full details are out: location, complete food and drink menu, operating hours, and a free collectible for the first guests on opening day.

Gideon's has one of the most cult-like followings of any Florida bakery — its Disney Springs location routinely draws lines — so a full restaurant under the same brand is a genuine event for parks foodies. If you want the opening-day freebie, plan to arrive early; grand openings at this brand tend to sell out fast.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Disney World's New Six Ravens Restaurant Sets Opening Date with Free Collectible

item.title: Bob Chapek's tell-all memoir bombs on arrival
item.description:
Former Disney CEO Bob Chapek's memoir — a tell-all covering his rise, his ouster, and his sense of being scapegoated — has reportedly flopped, with more people having watched a forgotten circa-2021 Disney+ show he greenlit than having read the book. It's the latest chapter in the ongoing "Bob swap" drama that has entertained Disney watchers for years.

Why it matters beyond the schadenfreude: the book's failure signals how thoroughly Chapek's era has been memory-holed, and how little appetite remains for re-litigating it. For Disney, it's one more closed door on a messy chapter; for Chapek, it's the end of the happily-ever-after arc. Expect the whole episode to fade fast.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Disgruntled Ex-Disney CEO Bob Chapek's Book Bombs

item.title: Disney World stacks dining deals: Candlelight packages and an Animal Kingdom lounge offer
item.description:
Walt Disney World rolled out two dining plays on the same day. First, the 2026 Candlelight Processional dining packages at EPCOT are on sale, with prices, participating restaurants, and reservation details announced for the beloved Festival of the Holidays tradition — and competition for these reservations is famously fierce, so booking early is the move.

Second, Animal Kingdom's standout Nomad Lounge is getting a $49 dining deal, new reservations, and dessert takeout — a direct attempt to fight the park's well-known afternoon exodus, when crowds thin out and the park empties. The takeaway: Disney is aggressively using food to smooth crowds and fill tables, and for visitors, both deals are real value plays worth checking if your trip dates line up.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: 2026 Candlelight Processional Dining Packages at Disney World: Prices, Restaurants & Top Picks
  • Disney Tourist Blog: Disney World's Best In-Park Lounge Adds $49 Dining Deal, Reservations & Dessert Takeout

item.title: A week after hiking pass prices, Disney adds a new Annual Passholder shopping perk
item.description:
Exactly one week after raising Walt Disney World Annual Pass prices by up to $120, Disney is trying to sweeten the pot: a new shopping discount for Passholders is part of a broader push to make APs feel valued again.

The timing is the story here. Passholders took the price increase hard, and Disney is now visibly pulling levers — perks and discounts — to repair the value proposition. Whether a shopping discount offsets a $120 hike is an open question, but the direction is clear: expect more targeted AP perks in the coming months as Disney works to keep its most loyal (and loudest) guests on board.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: New Shopping Discount for Disney World Passholders & Must-Buy Muppet Christmas Carol Merchandise

item.title: Mickey goes to the moon with Golden Goose; Muppets get Christmas merch
item.description:
Disney rolled out two notable merch drops. Mickey Mouse and friends are heading to the moon in a new collaboration with Golden Goose — a retro-futuristic, space-themed collection from the luxury sneaker brand known for its handcrafted, "perfectly imperfect" vintage aesthetic.

Separately, Muppets fans have reason to celebrate: a Muppet Christmas Carol merchandise line is arriving, timed for the holiday season. Both are limited-run plays in Disney's growing strategy of high-end designer collabs and nostalgia-driven holiday drops. If either is on your wish list, past experience says these sell out quickly.

Sources

  • Disney Parks Blog: Mickey & Friends Take Golden Goose to the Moon in New Collaboration
  • Disney Tourist Blog: New Shopping Discount for Disney World Passholders & Must-Buy Muppet Christmas Carol Merchandise

item.title: Disneyland raises ticket prices — but you can still beat the increase
item.description:
Disney raised prices for late-2026 and 2027 tickets on select Disneyland and California Adventure tickets, plus Park Hopper and Lightning Lane add-ons. That's the bad news. The good news: current prices are still available on discount tickets, so buying now locks in pre-increase rates for trips into next year.

Disney also dropped its 2026 holiday merchandise guide and a full Christmas 2026 planning guide for Walt Disney World — if you're going this December, the time to plan was yesterday.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Better Than Black Friday Sales: Disneyland Tickets at Discount Pre-Increase Prices for 2026 & 2027
  • Disney Parks Blog: 2026 Holiday Merchandise Guide: Merry Must-Haves for Everyone on Your List
  • Disney Tourist Blog: Disney World Christmas 2026 Ultimate Guide

item.title: Disney Treasure tests wearable Key to the World wristbands
item.description:
Guests aboard the Disney Treasure are participating in a test of wearable Key to the World wristbands that could expand to future Disney Cruise Line sailings — and possibly beyond the ships. It would bring cruise-line convenience in line with the MagicBand experience at the parks.

This is one to watch: if the test goes well, wristband entry and payments could become standard across Disney's cruise fleet.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Disney Treasure Tests Wearable Key to World Wristband

item.title: Disney+ casts leads for its Spaceship Earth TV pilot
item.description:
Disney+ has cast the leads for its pilot of a television series inspired by Spaceship Earth, the iconic EPCOT attraction. Adapting a slow-moving ride through the history of communication into a show is a creative swing — and a sign Disney is mining its parks IP for streaming content the way it mines everything else.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Disney’s Spaceship Earth TV Show Casts Leads

item.title: Disney x Gustaf Westman home collab, Cake Bake's $11 fries
item.description:
Designer Gustaf Westman is putting his signature spin on Mickey & Friends in a new line of Disney home goods — the most talked-about designer collab Disney's done in a while. Meanwhile, the Cake Bake Shop at Disney World keeps courting controversy: its new happy hour brings $11 fries, which fans say is exactly the kind of overpricing the restaurant has become known for.

One brand flex, one brand headache — both very Disney right now.

Sources

  • Disney Parks Blog: The Disney x Gustaf Westman Collab Will Make Your Home Decor Dreams Come True
  • Disney Tourist Blog: Cake Bake Happy Hour Brings $11 Fries to Disney World

item.title: Jollywood Nights sells out first night as holiday season heats up
item.description:
Disney Tourist Blog reports Jollywood Nights has sold out its first night early, while Mickey's Very Merry Christmas Party adds dates to meet demand.

The holiday-events arms race at Disney World continues — and the sellout pace suggests this year's seasonal offerings are striking a chord.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Jollywood Nights Sells Out First Night Early, as Mickey’s Very Merry Christmas Party Adds New Sold Out Dates

item.title: Lightning Lane prices hit new highs, with a $50 Premier Pass jump
item.description:
Disney World has raised Lightning Lane Single Pass prices to new highs, including a $50 increase on the Premier Pass, per Disney Tourist Blog.

It's the latest in the steady ratchet of skip-the-line pricing — and it keeps raising the question of how much more the parks can charge before the value proposition breaks.

Sources

  • Disney Tourist Blog: Disney World Raises Lightning Lane Single Pass Prices to New Highs, $50 Increase on Premier Pass Coming

item.title: Disney World's most polarizing price increase is closing a loophole
item.description:
Disney Tourist Blog reports on Disney World's most polarizing recent price increase — and how it's closing a loophole guests had been using to dodge it.

Disney pricing stories always generate heat, but the loophole-closing detail is the practical part: if you have a trip on the books, read this before you go so the change doesn't surprise you at checkout.

item.title: Every Disney World resort hotel, ranked worst to best
item.description:
Disney Tourist Blog ranks every Walt Disney World resort hotel from worst to best — the definitive planning reference whether you're booking your first trip or your fiftieth.

These rankings get updated as resorts renovate and prices shift, so it's worth checking even if you've read a previous version. The value picks in the middle tiers are usually where the interesting debate is.

item.title: First look at Monstropolis food, plus the show replacing MuppetVision
item.description:
Disney Tourist Blog shares a first look at the food coming to the new Monstropolis area, plus details on the show that will replace MuppetVision 3D.

The MuppetVision closure marks the end of an era — it was one of the last attractions with Jim Henson's direct involvement. The replacement has big shoes to fill, and the food preview suggests Disney is investing seriously in making Monstropolis a full land, not a facelift.
